about.title: San Clemente Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: San Clemente households rely daily on products ranging from car components to outdoor gear suited for its coastal, active lifestyle. When a manufacturing flaw, dangerous design, or missing warning label causes an injury, the resulting claim often falls under California's strict liability framework. That means an injured person generally doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. This applies whether the failure happened in a vehicle traveling along I-5, a tool used at home, or a product picked up at a local retailer along Avenida Pico. Multiple parties in the chain — manufacturer, distributor, retailer — may share responsibility. If you or someone in your family was hurt by a product in San Clemente, keeping the item itself and any packaging can matter a great deal later. LawProactive connects injured residents with an independent attorney, at no upfront cost, so they can explore what options may exist.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California often doesn't require proof of manufacturer negligence — just that the product was defective and caused injury, which can streamline what needs to be shown.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, giving an attorney more avenues to pursue on your behalf.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Because the defective item itself is often central evidence, an attorney can advise you early on how to keep it safe and untouched for review.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Many California product liability claims rely on strict liability, meaning the focus is on whether the product itself was defective and caused harm, not on the manufacturer's intent or care. An independent attorney can review your situation to see which legal theory applies.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try to keep the product exactly as it was at the time of the injury, along with any packaging, receipts, or instructions. This physical evidence is often important to an attorney evaluating a defect claim. Avoid attempting repairs or discarding any parts.

items.question: Does San Clemente have specific product liability concerns?
items.answer: With busy corridors like I-5, Avenida Pico, and El Camino Real seeing regular collisions, some product liability claims here involve defective vehicle parts or equipment failures connected to crashes. An attorney familiar with local patterns can help evaluate whether a product defect played a role.
